l.i: qui naturam tam fauentem habet, vt, siue ad
artem alibi deflectat, plus tamen tribuat na-
turæ: siue ab ea abeat nonnihil, ipsam vel
emendet, vel judicio commendet, quia non
ostentat. Sane vt nemo tantus nascitur ora-
tor quantus fit paulatim, quia lectione mul-
ta, quia eruditione, vsu, atque exercitatio-
ne opus est: ita, quod & de poëta vere dici-
tur, nemo fit orator summus qui non nasci-
tur. Magnus animus ac generosus, excitata
vis ingenii ac ardor, tum judicium quod ce-
tera absoluit, non parantur, sed diuinitus
contingunt. quo qui destituitur, corrumpit
quicquid legit, quia male concoquit quod
discit. quales sunt quos vmbra educat &
puluis. Qui, quemadmodum pictores primi
illi & adhuc ignari artis, si quid pingerent
aut inficete potius delinearent, nomen as-
scribebant, vt, quod arte, scilicet, non po-
terant, confessione, quæ quam maxime cum
arte pugnat, obtinerent; ita, nisi rheto-
rum præcepta non sequaris tantum, sed hoc
ipsum prope affcribas, præceptorum vel im-
memorem vel artis imperitum quidam
arbitantur. Quare & singulas quas dicee-

page.notes: Page signature "F" top right and running head "AD LECTOREM." are printed. The catchword "dice-" is printed at right below the last line; the text ends with "di-" at the line end, so the catchword is kept only as the bottom word. Ink blot over "& singulas" and the faint show-through are not transcribed. Italic type was used throughout the body; the copy above reflects the italic setting as read. Long s rendered as s. Possible doubtful readings: "affcribas" and "asscribebant" as printed.
